findings.claim: The selected archive is a completed paid Atria-Dawn-Preview campaign tied to source commit d7357092493f311f649a0742889b301d796911b5; the archive records the campaign repository as dirty.
findings.quantitative_result: ZIP SHA-256 e69dfc08ae988dada65e1b20a3674a5cb9282b3e98d1cdbdf84d4f15709b55dd; 2,968 members; 33/33 selected config hashes match the clean comparator snapshot.
findings.confidence: HIGH for archive identity, config-hash comparison, and recorded dirty flag; MEDIUM for source-snapshot association because the comparator is outside the ZIP.
alternatives: A different archive or a corrupted local copy could produce a misleading inventory if its hash were not verified.
A dirty working tree could have changed task/judge files without changing the selected config hashes.
limitations: Config equality is not byte-for-byte proof that all task, visible-test, judge, or helper code used in paid runs matches the clean snapshot.
The config comparison source path is an external /tmp snapshot and is not bundled as source code.
falsifiers: Re-hashing the designated origin/main ZIP yields a different SHA-256 or blob identity.
Recomputing any one of the 33 selected config hashes against the named clean source commit yields a mismatch.
findings.novelty: No scientific novelty claim; this is provenance and reproducibility groundwork.
follow_up_requirements: Archive the exact dirty diff or hash a complete rendered source bundle per case in any future run.
Keep the source comparator revision and hash table alongside the campaign artifact.

findings.claim: The campaign report records 194 scored selected cases and 24 separate pre-scoring omissions; the case manifest and result checkpoint contain the same 194 case IDs.
findings.quantitative_result: 194/194 selected results have status scored across 33 environments; 17 rope cases are omitted for unsupported provider input modality and 7 cases are omitted before provider access for known calibration failures; 218 case IDs are recorded as scored or explicitly omitted.
alternatives: The 218 total is the union of scored IDs and the two report omission lists, not an independently executed 218-row result table.
limitations: The 7 gate-blocked and 17 unsupported cases have no model score and must not be counted as failures or passes.
A complete unfiltered planned-design file is not required to reproduce this report-level union.
falsifiers: A duplicate or overlap between the two omission lists and the scored manifest.
A mismatch between the case IDs in pilot_manifest.json and suite_checkpoint.json.
findings.novelty: No scientific novelty claim; records coverage and exclusion scope.
follow_up_requirements: Make the planned, selected, omitted, and scored case sets separate first-class machine-readable records.
Report exclusion reason, disposition, and provider calls for every omitted case.

findings.claim: Two final selected results, not just the one named in the campaign-level outage counter, explicitly attribute their terminal failure to provider transients after bounded retries.
findings.quantitative_result: Raw checkpoint: 131 PASS / 63 FAIL among 194. Removing only report-listed ts_trajectory gives 131/193 PASS and 62 FAIL. Removing both final-note provider cases gives 131/192 PASS and 61 FAIL.
findings.confidence: HIGH that both final notes exist; MEDIUM that every terminal provider-coded row should be excluded from model-performance analysis, because the official campaign counter tracks only one episode.
alternatives: The campaign may define an outage episode more narrowly than any individual provider-transient error, in which case 131/193 matches its one named outage but leaves the second terminal provider-coded result mixed into FAIL.
The sheaf transient could be treated as an inconclusive infrastructure/model interaction rather than a scoreable model failure.
limitations: The raw row remains scored and its raw failure label is retained; the 192 denominator is an explicit analysis exclusion, not a rewritten campaign report.
API error events also include transient retries that recovered; only final-result terminal notes define these two exclusions.
falsifiers: The exact phrase is absent from one of the two final.json files or is attached to a different case/run.
A verified terminal model submission for the sheaf row shows that the provider note was not causal to its final failure.
findings.novelty: A case-level reporting inconsistency in this archive; not a general provider-reliability result.
follow_up_requirements: Separate provider/network termination from invalid model action in the result schema.
Have campaign_report aggregate every final result note and provide per-case outage/retry scope.
Preserve raw and sensitivity denominators in any post.

findings.claim: The campaign contains two materially different scoring-guarantee groups, and the report excludes compile-only results from a validated aggregate.
findings.quantitative_result: Raw: 72 behavioral_reference rows with 56 PASS/16 FAIL; 122 compile_only rows with 75 PASS/47 FAIL. After excluding both provider-coded terminal rows, compile_only is 120 rows with 75 PASS/45 FAIL; behavioral_reference remains 72 with 56/16.
findings.confidence: HIGH for the labels, counts, and report disclaimer.
alternatives: Per-instance calibration records may provide useful evidence about specific validators even where a row is labelled compile_only; the archive's group-level disclaimer still applies.
Behavioral_reference should not be equated with an independent external oracle; the instance preflight can share judge code paths.
limitations: Only epistemic_games has an environment-level public_bayes_oracle behavioral self-test recorded as executed/passed.
The exact-instance per-case calibration and environment-level oracle preflight are separate mechanisms.
falsifiers: A re-read of campaign_report.json or the per-case guarantee fields yields different counts or no compile-only disclaimer.
findings.novelty: No novelty claim; this is an interpretation constraint on campaign totals.
follow_up_requirements: Always publish per-mode counts and a calibration/preflight description.
Use explicit labels for judge family, exact-instance reference availability, and independent validation status.

findings.claim: The archive assigns all seven epistemic_games cases to the recorded ml_debugging track, although the inspected task core implements symbolic Bayesian inference.
findings.quantitative_result: Recorded track summary: ml_debugging 37 cases, 16 PASS/21 FAIL. Source-semantic regrouping: 30 ML-debugging cases, 9 PASS/21 FAIL; epistemic_games separate at 7/7 PASS.
findings.confidence: HIGH for recorded label; HIGH that task semantics are symbolic Bayesian inference in the comparator; MEDIUM for whether the recorded grouping was intentionally multi-purpose.
alternatives: The track could denote campaign ordering or execution infrastructure rather than scientific task family. No archive field documents such a dual meaning.
limitations: The analysis_family override is an explicit editorial regrouping; the raw track is preserved unchanged.
A dirty source tree limits claims about the exact executed task code.
falsifiers: Campaign documentation showing that `ml_debugging` intentionally includes epistemic_games as a stable cross-family grouping.
A different archived environment implementation for epistemic_games.
findings.novelty: A data-labeling correction in this campaign, not a model result.
follow_up_requirements: Validate environment-to-track mappings against task metadata before aggregation.
Store conceptual family separately from execution track.

findings.claim: Selected nominal-axis outcomes are heterogeneous and sometimes nonmonotone; the archived `easy`/`medium`/`hard` labels do not form a common calibrated scalar difficulty scale.
findings.quantitative_result: Examples: regex at easy surface passes at lengths 32/128/512, while medium/hard surface labels fail at length 32; CSS at easy surface scores 0.416667/0/1.0 over 3/4/5 bits (the middle row is source-invalid); SQL at easy surface passes at graph-chain lengths 6 and 25 but has a source-invalid length-12 case; moco visible-test levels are pass/fail/pass.
findings.confidence: HIGH for these observed case outcomes; LOW for any causal effect of a nominal axis.
alternatives: Sampling variation at temperature 1.0 can produce different outcomes across one-run cells.
Class-name substitutions, hints, source validation, and other unrecorded dirty-source changes can explain differences.
A hard level may alter multiple effective properties or leave an axis unimplemented.
limitations: One selected case/seed per cell and no cell-level replications.
Many comparisons are one-factor contrasts around a single baseline, not full factorial designs.
Axis names such as hidden_depth map to different quantities in different environments.
falsifiers: Repeated randomized runs with semantically equivalent stimuli show no stable response pattern.
Rendered prompt/judge hashes show the presumed axis did not change or changed additional confounds.
findings.novelty: No methodological novelty claim; at most a task/model-specific response pattern.
follow_up_requirements: Verify rendered diffs for every axis level and reject unused axes.
Run repeated seeds with matched names/hints and independent task instances.
Use task-specific size labels instead of a shared nominal difficulty vocabulary.

findings.claim: Atria-Dawn-Preview returned fully correct answers on the seven selected epistemic_games instances, whose source defines Bayesian inference over two specified behavioral policies rather than a recursive level-k process.
findings.quantitative_result: 7/7 PASS, score 1.0; each final result records exact posterior credit, correct likelihood-ratio verdict, correct most-supported world, provenance_ok=true, and all_correct=true. The selected exact posteriors include 1/2, 3/5, 1/15, and 92/177.
findings.confidence: HIGH for the recorded task-level outcomes and source-described target; MEDIUM for generalization to the executed tree due dirty-source provenance.
alternatives: The model may have recognized a formula or task pattern rather than performing a general Bayesian procedure.
The answer may reflect an exact deterministic calculation task rather than social or strategic reasoning.
limitations: Seven instances, one seed, one model/configuration; only one solo presentation and one skewed prior.
The policies and likelihood tables are stipulated and public; there is no recursively generated strategic agent with utilities and alternating beliefs.
falsifiers: Recomputing any archived final metric shows a failed correctness check or a posterior mismatch.
A clean rerun on the exact items fails to reproduce the 7/7 result.
findings.novelty: No broad ToM or Bayesian benchmark novelty claim; a narrow result on these seven cases.
follow_up_requirements: Separate fixed-policy Bayesian calibration from explicit recursive ToM in task taxonomy and reporting.
Test unseen policy likelihoods, multiple seeds, varied observation channels, and generated higher-order belief recursion.

findings.claim: The category_theoretic_compositional track is a heterogeneous code-repair set with mixed judge guarantees, not a homogeneous test of category-theoretic reasoning.
findings.quantitative_result: 85 raw rows; one provider-coded row excluded; 57 PASS/27 FAIL among 84 eligible rows. Eligible mode split: 4/5 PASS for categorical_lenses behavioral_reference and 53/79 PASS for compile_only cases. The 17-environment track spans task families with outcomes from 0/5 to 5/5.
findings.confidence: HIGH for counts and source-semantic heterogeneity; MEDIUM for task categorization under dirty-source provenance.
alternatives: The `category_theoretic_compositional` label may be an engineering grouping rather than a formal mathematical claim.
Some tasks can validly test finite algebraic laws even without broad category-theoretic competence.
limitations: 79 eligible cases are compile-only, and the exact behavioral-reference cases are only a subset.
Several axes are not referenced in the clean comparator; some prompts/judges have scope mismatches.
The campaign's source dirty flag blocks complete executed-implementation attribution.
falsifiers: A recovered dirty-source snapshot shows every compared task/judge implemented the advertised mathematical property and independent validation covers all eligible cases.
A more precise source definition of track membership shows the group was intended only as a non-theoretical software-engineering category.
findings.novelty: No category-theory capability or mathematical-theory novelty claim; the result is a benchmark audit and task-level outcome inventory.
follow_up_requirements: Define an explicit property per task, anchor semantics in the public prompt, and test counterexamples/valid alternatives.
Replace compile-only scoring with independent behavioral references or keep those rows explicitly exploratory.
Fix or remove axis placeholders that are not consumed by task/judge templates.

findings.claim: The scalar PASS/FAIL and failure-mode labels conceal materially different terminal events, including empty patches, source-validation failures, runtime failures, malformed actions, provider transients, and missing required companion files.
findings.quantitative_result: Among 192 eligible cases, 61 fails: 24 patch_invalid (all empty patches), 20 underfit, 10 source_invalid, 3 runtime_error, 2 invalid_action, and 2 overfit_visible_tests. The latter two are labeled overfit but have trusted_score=1.0 and missing required-file notes. Two provider-coded final rows are outside this taxonomy denominator.
findings.confidence: HIGH for terminal notes/metrics and counts; MEDIUM for mapping those terminal labels to latent reasoning failures.
alternatives: Some patch or source-validation errors may be partly induced by the action interface, patch validator, or task constraints rather than the underlying task concept.
An empty final patch may follow model termination, tool failure, or an unobserved serialization issue; the final artifact alone does not isolate cause.
limitations: `failure_mode` is a campaign/judge label; it is not a validated taxonomy of cognitive mechanisms.
The `overfit_visible_tests` label does not match the recorded notes in two cases.
falsifiers: Reinspection of the linked final patches or judge metrics contradicts the empty-patch/missing-file classifications.
A separately validated adjudication reclassifies the failure modes with independent evidence.
findings.novelty: Failure-layer separation is a useful reporting correction, not a novel theory of model failure.
follow_up_requirements: Separate submission/patch, source-validation, action-protocol, infrastructure, runtime, and behavioral-test failure states.
Audit taxonomy labels against judge notes before publishing them.
Report score, trusted score, failed checks, and raw patch hash for each failure class.

findings.claim: The weird_machine track shows task-specific successes and failures under regex, CSS, SQL, spreadsheet, CI, and template tasks; the controlled surface/depth pattern is especially sharp in regex but confounded and unreplicated.
findings.quantitative_result: 25/30 eligible PASS overall. Regex 3/5; CSS 3/5; SQL 4/5; spreadsheet 5/5; CI dependency graph 5/5; template interpreter 5/5. At easy regex surface, all 3 string lengths pass; at easy string length, the other 2 class-name variants fail.
findings.confidence: HIGH for the selected case outcomes; LOW for generalized surface/depth causality.
alternatives: Class-name cues, the hard-level performance note, sampling at temperature 1.0, source validation, or hidden-source differences may drive the observed cells.
The `hidden_depth` axis denotes different input-size proxies rather than a common measure of reasoning depth.
limitations: One run per selected cell, no seed-level replication, and only a sparse design.
The regex surface manipulation bundles class name and an extra hard-level hint.
CSS and SQL selected failures include source-validation errors.
falsifiers: Repeated matched-name/hint trials fail to reproduce the regex contrast.
Rendered workspace/task hashes show the hypothesized axis did not change as expected.
findings.novelty: No general computational-substrate claim; only a cohort/task-specific observation.
follow_up_requirements: Separate names, hints, and input-size manipulations in a factorial design.
Replicate across seeds and independently generated inputs.
Report exact judge checks and failure layers per case.

findings.claim: The recurrent-depth family has high recorded pass counts, but the environment and judge-mode mixture does not establish a general recurrence-depth scaling law.
findings.quantitative_result: 31/33 PASS; rd_state_carry 11/11 behavioral_reference, rd_gradient_credit 11/11 compile_only, rd_adaptive_halting 9/11 compile_only. The adaptive easy-depth failure is an unexpected-indentation source error; another failure is a float-mask runtime error.
findings.confidence: HIGH for recorded counts and terminal notes; LOW for a depth-related mechanism.
alternatives: Patch syntax/runtime failures may be independent of recurrence depth.
Compile-only cases may pass the implemented checks without demonstrating generalization to unseen recurrence structures.
limitations: Mixed behavioral-reference/compile-only guarantees and one seed per selected case.
The depth manipulation changes several numerical capacities and is not replicated.
falsifiers: A controlled multi-seed sweep with identical non-depth inputs shows a stable monotone/degrading trend or no trend.
An independently validated hidden-depth oracle reveals systematic behavioral errors in current PASS rows.
findings.novelty: No scaling-law claim; task-level output inventory only.
follow_up_requirements: Separate source-validity, runtime, and behavioral correctness outcomes.
Use held-out recurrence depths and independent oracle tests across repeated seeds.

findings.claim: After removing the epistemic_games track-label anomaly, the three selected ML-debugging environments show 9/30 PASS, with highly uneven task outcomes.
findings.quantitative_result: batchnorm_ema 0/11 (compile_only), glyph 0/8 (behavioral_reference), moco 9/11 (behavioral_reference); the two MoCo/BatchNorm rows labeled overfit_visible_tests have notes about missing required companion files.
findings.confidence: HIGH for per-environment result counts and notes; MEDIUM for using the three tasks as a coherent ML-debugging construct.
alternatives: The track may be an administrative grouping rather than a coherent task family.
The compile-only BatchNorm results are not directly comparable to the reference-labeled Glyph/MoCo results.
limitations: Only three environment families are grouped here; one has compile-only judgments.
One seed and one selected response per case; no general ML-debugging inference.
falsifiers: A documented track schema assigns epistemic_games intentionally to this group or identifies additional debugging environments omitted from the source-semantic grouping.
follow_up_requirements: Repair family mappings and compare judge modes separately.
Audit required-file and visible-test coverage before assigning overfit labels.

findings.claim: The archive contains incompatible retry counters and a reasoning-mode metadata discrepancy; usage or retry totals should not be collapsed into a single canonical value.
findings.quantitative_result: All 268 runs: 4,061 successful responses, 4,023 summed run/turn IDs, 9,447,242 successful-response tokens. `reasoning_enabled=false` coexists with 325,785 reported reasoning tokens and 2,710 rows containing a reasoning_content field. Retry counts range by source/scope from 3,869 selected final-manifest attempts to 6,412 progress-reported attempts.
findings.confidence: HIGH that the archived counters/fields disagree; LOW about the underlying cause.
alternatives: Different counters may intentionally count distinct layers, retries, successes, or checkpoint scopes.
A provider may populate reasoning usage fields independently of the request's reasoning_enabled setting.
limitations: No spend/cost field exists in the exported archive.
No reasoning content is copied or interpreted; presence counts are metadata only.
falsifiers: A documented counter contract reconciles all totals without missing/duplicate events.
A canonical run manifest explains why reasoning fields appear when the setting is false.
findings.novelty: A provenance/telemetry discrepancy in this archive, not a cognitive finding.
follow_up_requirements: Define request, HTTP-attempt, retry, response, and turn counters separately.
Persist exact request configuration and provider response metadata with consistency checks.
Keep raw logs and do not copy hidden reasoning text into public artifacts.

findings.claim: The category-track source comparator indicates several advertised axes were not implemented in the environment templates, so nominal coverage can overstate the number of distinct interventions.
findings.quantitative_result: The static scan finds ten no-reference control/variable axes across nine category environments, including both axes in compositional_optimizer; details are in axis_placeholder_audit.csv and source_implementation_audit.md.
findings.confidence: HIGH for no direct reference in the inspected clean source files; MEDIUM for the claim about executed paid cases because the recorded repository was dirty.
alternatives: An unarchived dirty-source change, external generator behavior, or indirect runtime key use could implement a control not apparent from the clean file scan.
Some axes may be metadata-only labels rather than intended interventions.
limitations: The static scan does not execute generation or compare every rendered task bundle.
Only selected configurations were scanned; unsupported and gate-blocked cases were not model-run.
falsifiers: A rendered-task diff or recovered dirty source shows the axis values altered the agent task or judge despite no clean-template reference.
findings.novelty: Potentially useful in-repository benchmark QA, not a general scientific finding.
follow_up_requirements: Add an axis linter that verifies each level changes a declared agent-visible or judge-visible artifact.
Save per-level rendered diffs and block campaigns on no-op controls.

findings.claim: The inspected source comparator contains task/judge mismatches that materially limit interpretation of category-family pass rates.
findings.quantitative_result: Compositional optimizer prompt promises nested associativity/multiple steps while judge checks shape and one state-isolation chain; physical constraints judge enforces an unstated 5:3 ratio; categorical-lens hidden judge checks laws but does not itself assert coordinate-zero view, while the visible test does.
findings.confidence: HIGH for line-level source-comparator observations; MEDIUM for executed-run attribution due dirty source.
alternatives: The benchmark author may intend the judge as a deliberately narrow proxy rather than a full implementation of the prompt claim.
Visible tests/starter-code defaults can reveal some otherwise unstated expectations to the model.
limitations: These audit examples do not prove that every category task is under-specified.
The lens visible test partly anchors the first-coordinate convention even though the hidden judge does not assert it directly.
falsifiers: A recovered executed source snapshot changes the cited prompt, visible tests, or judge so the mismatch disappears.
A formal task specification makes the narrower judge criteria explicit and intended.
findings.novelty: No mathematical-theory novelty; this is task/judge contract QA.
follow_up_requirements: Align prompts, visible tests, judges, and reference implementations before score interpretation.
Test valid alternatives and adversarial counterexamples with an independent oracle.

findings.claim: The most defensible synthesis is a descriptive map of task-specific result and failure patterns, not a scalar measure of general reasoning capability.
findings.quantitative_result: Family counts range from 2/8 eligible PASS in trajectory synthesis to 31/33 in recurrent depth, while judge guarantees, task sizes, no-op axes, and failure modes vary; no common score calibration is demonstrated.
findings.confidence: HIGH as a reporting recommendation; MEDIUM as a theoretical interpretation.
alternatives: A future benchmark calibration could establish a common latent trait or comparable judge behavior, but none is present in this archive.
limitations: The archive measures one model/provider/configuration, with one seed per selected instance and mixed grading modes.
The same model may have different sampling variance across environments and retries.
falsifiers: A replicated, calibrated multi-task study demonstrates measurement invariance and a reliable common latent score across judge modes.
findings.novelty: No general capability or latent-trait claim.
follow_up_requirements: Validate judges independently, define common scoring semantics, and estimate repeatability before comparing family-level capability.

findings.claim: The cited prior work already covers broad multi-scenario/multi-metric evaluation, variable perturbation, controlled epistemic-logic tasks, recursive ToM/deception, causal-template ToM generation, and test-coverage limits in code-agent evaluation.
findings.quantitative_result: HELM reports 42 scenarios and multiple metrics; VarBench applies dynamic variable perturbation and five seeds for variable-based experiments; MindGames uses dynamic epistemic logic; Hi-ToM studies higher-order recursive beliefs/deception; BigToM uses causal templates; the SWE-bench empirical study reports 7.8% of plausible patches counted correct failing the full developer test suite in its studied setting.
findings.confidence: HIGH for the cited paper abstracts/metadata and the narrow precedent summaries; LOW for any exhaustive novelty conclusion.
alternatives: The exact combination of this generator, model, tasks, and archive may be under-studied; the current search did not establish global precedence or uniqueness.
limitations: This is a targeted prior-work check, not a systematic literature review.
External prior-work findings do not directly establish correctness or error in the current archive.
falsifiers: A broader, reproducible literature review finds no prior work covering a specific narrowly worded contribution.
findings.novelty: No broad novelty claim survives; only a cohort-specific empirical audit may be distinctive.
follow_up_requirements: If making a novelty claim, conduct a systematic related-work search and define the comparison set, task scope, and method precisely.

findings.claim: In this particular regex task and model run, surface class names or the hard-level performance hint may have influenced the two failures more than the tested input-string length; this is an untested hypothesis, not an inferred causal effect.
findings.quantitative_result: At easy surface, selected lengths 32, 128, and 512 all pass. At string length 32, the medium and hard surface variants fail with output lengths 34 and 66. The hard prompt adds a performance note.
alternatives: The difference may be sampling noise from one seed at temperature 1.0.
The names, performance note, input length, or hidden-source differences may interact; the current design cannot identify a dominant factor.
limitations: Only five selected rows from one model/configuration; no repeated seed per cell.
Surface label bundles class-name changes and an added hard-level hint.
The clean comparator is not proven identical to the dirty paid-run source.
falsifiers: Matched multi-seed trials show no stable effect of class-name/hint changes at fixed size.
A separate size-only experiment produces a larger reproducible effect than surface changes.
findings.novelty: No novelty or general weird-machine claim; a hypothesis to guide a controlled follow-up.
follow_up_requirements: Run the E2 factorial follow-up with independent seeds and generated equivalent inputs.
Predefine the primary contrast and report behavioral, patch-validity, and source/runtime outcomes separately.
